# internal.txt: declarations that stay internal although their name is in
# allow-api.txt. Each shares its name with an allowed declaration (`html`,
# `select`, `valueOf`, `index`, `subscript`, `outerHtml`) but has a type in
# its signature that is itself internal, which Swift refuses on a public
# declaration ("cannot be declared public because its parameter uses an
# internal type"). The compiler found them in the first campaign; a new
# SwiftSoup release may add or drop some: the script stops when a line here
# is not in the release, and the compiler names a declaration that must be
# added.
#
# Format: File.swift: the declaration's line as the release has it, without
# its indentation (and without the `@inline(__always)` line before it).
Attribute.swift: public func html(accum: StringBuilder, out: OutputSettings) {
Attributes.swift: public func html(accum: StringBuilder, out: OutputSettings ) throws {
Element.swift: public func select(_ evaluator: Evaluator)throws->Elements {
Element.swift: open override func html(_ appendable: StringBuilder) throws -> StringBuilder {
Elements.swift: open func select(_ evaluator: Evaluator)throws->Elements {
Node.swift: public func outerHtml(_ accum: StringBuilder) throws {
Node.swift: open func html(_ appendable: StringBuilder)throws -> StringBuilder {
OrderedSet.swift: public func index(of object: T) -> Index? {
OrderedSet.swift: public subscript(index: Index) -> T {
Tag.swift: public static func valueOf(_ tagName: String, _ settings: ParseSettings) throws -> Tag {
Tag.swift: public static func valueOf(_ tagName: [UInt8], _ settings: ParseSettings) throws -> Tag {
Whitelist.swift: public func == (lhs: TypedValue, rhs: TypedValue) -> Bool {
